subject: design-studies
title: Ergonomic Dimensions: Fit the Chair and Desk to the Student

questions.prompt: A student says: One standard size fits every user, because a chair built to average measurements fits each person who sits in it. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - if everyone can sit on the chair, it fits everyone

Ergonomic design sizes the product from the user own measurements: the seat height is set to the lower-leg height so the feet rest flat, the seat width to the hip breadth plus clearance, and the desk height to the seat height plus the seated elbow height.
A standard chair fits everyone because averages are measured from real people
The chair should be built to the tallest student so nobody is too big for it

questions.misconception: One standard size fits every user, because a chair built to average measurements fits each person who sits in it.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: One standard size fits every user, because a chair built to average measurements fits each person who sits in it. In fact ergonomic design sizes the product from the student own measurements: seat height 40 cm equals the lower-leg height so the feet rest flat, seat width is hip breadth 36 cm plus 4 cm clearance, and desk height is seat height 40 cm plus the seated elbow height of 24 cm.

questions.prompt: Which measurement sets the seat height of an ergonomic chair?

choices.text: The average seat height of all chairs in the classroom
The lower-leg height of the user, so the feet rest flat on the floor
The height of the desk the chair will be used with
The hip breadth of the user plus clearance

questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: the seat rises until its height equals the lower-leg height of 40 cm, and the feet rest flat.

questions.prompt: A student has seat height 40 cm and seated elbow height 24 cm. Calculate the desk height and state what sets it.
questions.answer: Desk height = seat height + seated elbow height = 40 + 24 = 64 cm, set so the forearms rest level on the desk top.
questions.explanation: Scene 3 runs this: the desk top settles at the seat height plus the seated elbow height.

questions.prompt: Explain why the fit bar climbs as the chair is sized in the animation.
questions.answer: Each dimension set from a measurement closes one fit gap - seat height first, then seat width, then desk height - so the bar climbs by one third at each stage and fills only when every dimension fits the student.
questions.explanation: The fit bar rises in s2 and s3 and fills in s4: one climb per gap closed.

questions.prompt: A student has hip breadth 36 cm. With 4 cm of clearance, what seat width should be built?

choices.text: 36 cm: exactly the hip breadth, with no room to spare
50 cm: a standard width that suits most students

questions.explanation: Scene 3 works this sum: the seat widens to the hip breadth plus clearance, 36 + 4 = 40 cm.
